blocks.text: JAHAZIEL THE LEVITE, “OF THE SONS OF ASAPH” · TWO KINGDOMS
Jahaziel. In the assembly before Jehoshaphat: “the battle is not yours, but God’s.”
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophet
ERA
Two kingdoms 930–586 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
Jehoshaphat
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
“Then upon Jahaziel … came the Spirit of the LORD in the midst of the congregation”; he spoke with “Thus saith the LORD unto you”.
THE CALL
How the word came
“Then upon Jahaziel … came the Spirit of the LORD in the midst of the congregation”; he spoke with “Thus saith the LORD unto you”. 2 Chronicles 20:14–15
BEFORE THE KINGS
Before Jehoshaphat
KING OF JUDAH
Jehoshaphat
“Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.”
2 Chronicles 20:15 (KJV) →
THE MESSAGE
The word in its main themes
The battle is God's
“for the battle is not yours, but God’s.”
2 Chronicles 20:15 (KJV) →
Stand still and see
“set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the salvation of the LORD with you, O Judah and Jerusalem”
2 Chronicles 20:17 (KJV) →
THE WORD TO …
To whom the word was spoken
TO ALL JUDAH, JERUSALEM AND KING JEHOSHAPHAT
“Hearken ye, all Judah, and ye inhabitants of Jerusalem, and thou king Jehoshaphat”
2 Chronicles 20:15 (KJV) →
COMPANIONS AND OPPONENTS
Who stood with him, and against him
Asaph
Zechariah, his father
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
From the textScripture names Jahaziel only here. 2 Chronicles 20:14
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 1
2 Chronicles 20
PASSAGES · 2
2 Chronicles 20:14–17 2 Chronicles 20:20–26
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Kings does not tell this war or Jahaziel's word; it is in Chronicles only.
Chronicles does not use the words “according to the word of the LORD” of the victory; it tells what happened next.
Nothing else is told of Jahaziel.
